blocks.title: Vehicle import requirements, duties and process in Kenya
blocks.body: Kenya remains one of East Africa's largest markets for imported vehicles. Whether you're importing a car from Japan, a 4x4 from UAE, or a commercial vehicle from South Africa, Kenya Tradex helps manage the shipping, compliance, customs, inspection and registration steps required before the vehicle reaches the road legally.
paragraphs: Looking to ship other goods? See our ocean freight services , our South Africa vehicle import guide , or shipping from Dubai .
items: Vehicle Shipping: Roll-on/Roll-off (RoRo) or container shipping from Japan, UAE, UK, and South Africa.
QISJ Pre-Shipment Inspection: Coordination with QISJ for vehicle inspection at origin before shipping.
Customs Clearance: Full KRA processing at Mombasa port - import duty, excise duty, VAT, and IDF fees based on engine capacity.
Door-to-Door Delivery: We deliver vehicles to Nairobi, Kampala, Kigali, and other regional destinations after customs clearance.
NTSA Registration: Road registration and number plate acquisition support.

blocks.title: Kenya Vehicle Import Requirements
items: Right-Hand Drive (RHD) Only: Kenya only permits Right-Hand Drive vehicles. Left-Hand Drive vehicles are not allowed, regardless of age or condition.
Maximum Age: Used passenger vehicles must not exceed 8 years from the year of manufacture.
QISJ Pre-Shipment Inspection: All vehicles must be inspected at origin by QISJ (Quality Inspection Services Japan). A valid QISJ certificate is required for customs clearance in Kenya.

KEBS Local Inspection Surcharge: If a vehicle arrives without a QISJ inspection certificate, KEBS charges a 5% surcharge for local inspection. Pre-shipment inspection is strongly recommended to avoid additional costs.
NTSA Registration: All vehicles must be registered with National Transport and Safety Authority before road use.

Avoiding Problem Vehicles: Be cautious when buying from markets like Dubai where accident-repaired vehicles are common. Always request a pre-purchase inspection report before committing to a purchase.

blocks.title: How to import a vehicle to Kenya
items: Step 1: Purchase your Right-Hand Drive vehicle and obtain original logbook and invoice from the seller. Be cautious of accident-repaired vehicles, especially from markets like Dubai.

Step 2: Book a pre-shipment inspection with QISJ (Quality Inspection Services Japan). A valid QISJ certificate is required for smooth customs clearance and avoids a 5% KEBS surcharge for local inspection.
Step 3: Book shipping through Kenya Tradex. Choose RoRo or container shipping based on your vehicle and budget.
Step 4: Kenya Tradex applies for KRA Import Declaration Form (IDF) before cargo arrives.
Step 5: Customs clearance at Mombasa port - Kenya Tradex handles duty payments and documentation. Present your QISJ certificate to avoid the KEBS local inspection surcharge.
Step 6: NTSA road registration and door-to-door delivery to Nairobi, Kampala, Kigali, or your preferred location.

blocks.title: Vehicle import questions
items:
Can I import a used car to Kenya? 
Yes, but only Right-Hand Drive vehicles are permitted. Left-Hand Drive vehicles are not allowed in Kenya regardless of age. Used vehicles must be under 8 years old and require a valid QISJ inspection certificate. Kenya Tradex handles the entire import process from origin to door-to-door delivery.

What are the import duties for cars in Kenya? 
Kenya charges a flat import duty of 35% of the customs value for all vehicles, regardless of engine capacity. Additionally, imported vehicles attract Excise duty (20-35% depending on engine size and fuel type), VAT (16%), and IDF fees. Contact Kenya Tradex for a detailed cost estimate.

How long does it take to import a car to Kenya? 
Import time varies by origin: Japan takes 20-30 days, UAE 7-12 days, UK 20-30 days, and South Africa 7-14 days. After arrival at Mombasa, customs clearance typically takes 3-7 days. Total process: 3-6 weeks depending on origin and documentation readiness.

What documents do I need to import a vehicle to Kenya? 
Required documents include: Original Bill of Lading, Commercial Invoice, Packing List, KRA Import Declaration Form (IDF), and a valid QISJ inspection certificate. Note: Export certificate of origin is not required. Kenya Tradex handles the customs clearance process.

Can returning residents import a vehicle duty-free? 
Yes. Kenyan citizens who have resided abroad for 12 months or more may qualify for duty-free vehicle import under specific Kenya Customs conditions. Key requirements: the vehicle must have been owned and used abroad for at least 12 months prior to import; the importer must return to Kenya and clear the car through customs within 3 months of their arrival; and during the 12 months abroad, the person must not have spent more than 90 days in Kenya. Kenya Tradex assists returning residents with eligibility assessment and documentation for duty-free clearance.
